title: Dispatch TUR 8: Last Westmere Train Arrives Twelve Years Early
summary: Passengers from a future evacuation reach the platform built for them in Alderwick.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: At 11:54 last night, the goods yard filled with coal smoke. Witnesses saw neither rails nor an approaching engine until the first carriage passed the line of red lamps. Then a train stood against the timber platform, its wheels submerged in dark water that did not spread beyond the trestles.

Guard Amos Pell opened the nearest door. He called for assistance before asking what year it was. Volunteers led 106 passengers into the yard. All appeared to have travelled from the evacuation of Kingsfen on 17 October 1894. The last carriage was empty. A minute after its door was checked, the locomotive bell rang and the train withdrew into the smoke. The platform clock resumed ticking.

Miriam Harrow recognized her mother at once. Mrs. Harrow had to ask the child’s name. They stood together beneath the yellow umbrella until a physician brought Miriam inside. Theo Wren, aged ten, met the grandfather who had drawn the platform and the father who has not yet seen his birth. The family has requested privacy.

Dr. Saye warned that the passengers’ arrival does not establish what will happen in 1894. The marsh flood may still occur; an evacuation may still be required. Guard Pell says the bridge failed behind the train, but the platform appeared ahead in time for him to give the order to continue.

No passenger was lost at Alderwick. In the yard this morning, Mr. Pike counted 106 names against Pell’s list and placed the letters in order beside the timetable plate. Mr. Wren’s oldest plan was dated 1881. The newest letter was still damp.
